Investors are paying tech stock prices for detergent and diapers.

Procter & Gamble ( PG ), the maker of Tide, Pampers, and Charmin, had its best day since March 2020 on Thursday, adding more than $20 billion in market value. The stock closed at its highest level since February, just shy of its 2026 high, even as the broader market slid.

P&G gave investors exactly what they wanted: steady growth. Sales rose 4% in its fiscal first quarter, mostly because people bought more of its products. The unit that makes Tide and P&G's other cleaning products grew 5%. The company also stuck with its full-year outlook.

"The consumer is with us," CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance on Thursday. In a market searching for safety, that was enough.

P&G now costs more than some of the biggest names in tech.

Investors often gauge how expensive a stock is using the price-to-earnings ratio (P/E), which divides the stock price by the company's earnings per share. Using next year's expected earnings, P&G trades at about 22 times. That's more than Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta ( META ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ), which trade at less than two-thirds of P&G's multiple.

Tech stocks have been getting cheaper because Wall Street is penciling in stronger future earnings, which makes the "E" in P/E get bigger and the ratio smaller. The recent tech sell-off has knocked down their stock prices, also lowering valuations.

P&G investors are paying a hefty price for a company expecting earnings growth of 3% at most this year.

So why pay up? Investors are paying for predictability. People keep buying toothpaste and toilet paper no matter what the economy does, so P&G's earnings rarely surprise to the downside. When markets get rocky, that kind of reliability becomes more valuable.

P&G isn't alone. Kimberly-Clark ( KMB ), the maker of Kleenex and Huggies, and Colgate-Palmolive ( CL ) each gained 4% to 5% on Thursday, and Coca-Cola ( KO ) closed at a record.

The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLP ), which holds the household names people shop for every week, just had its best 13-day run since April 2020. Thursday alone was its best day since April 2025. Over the same stretch, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has slipped and chip stocks have taken a beating .

Falling interest rates are also helping. Staples stocks are often treated like bonds because they pay steady dividends. When Treasury yields fall, as they did sharply on Thursday , those dividends look more attractive by comparison.

articles.title: Chipotle’s Softening Sales Force Analyst to Throw in the Towel
articles.summary: A long-standing Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. bull has moved to the sidelines, citing concern that a slow start to the fourth quarter suggests softer sales for...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- A long-standing Chipotle Mexican Grill Inc. bull has moved to the sidelines, citing concern that a slow start to the fourth quarter suggests softer sales for the year ahead.

TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles lowered his recommendation on the shares to hold from buy on Wednesday, just ahead of the burrito maker's earnings report next week. He also cut his 12-month price target to a Street-low $32 from $44, while his bear case assumes the stock could drop to $25 per share.

Charles says that while Chipotle's third-quarter results should be slightly better than consensus, medium-term same-store sales forecasts are too high as the brand relies less on price increases to prioritize growing traffic.

"The start of the quarter is showing underlying softness at a time when the business ought to be clicking," Charles, who'd held a buy-equivalent rating on Chipotle since 2019, said in an interview. "Now that we believe that it's more likely Chipotle is going to miss 2027 estimates more materially, we thought now is a good time to move to the sidelines."

Chipotle shares have shed 24% this year and are trading near a three-year low, making it one of the worst performers in the S&P Composite 1500 Restaurants Index, which is down 6.6% in 2026. Restaurant stocks have broadly struggled amid deteriorating consumer sentiment.

Chipotle has seen some success in assuring customers who've grown weary of high-priced "slop bowls" that its prices are justified, an issue that triggered sales declines in recent quarters. The company's latest earnings release showed sales performed better than expected thanks to buzz around limited-time offers like honey chicken, in addition to promotions via its loyalty app.

Still, Charles fears these initiatives may not be enough to overpower macro headwinds while warning that other sales drivers such as high-efficiency kitchen equipment and catering are "less proven," setting the stage for a challenging 2027.

TD Cowen lowered its fourth-quarter same-store sales growth estimate to 1% from 4%, well below the 2.9% gain analysts polled by Bloomberg are expecting. Charles's 2027 projection was cut to 2.1% from 3.8%, compared with the consensus estimate of a 3.1% increase.

articles.title: Apple could be about to dethrone Nvidia as world's most valuable company
articles.summary: A Big Tech battle to watch on Friday: Apple vs. Nvidia's market cap.
articles.body:
Tough reviews of Apple's ( AAPL ) new foldable Duo smartphone don't appear to be shaking the bulls on the stock.

Apple's market cap of $5.08 trillion is less than 1% shy of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) $5.12 trillion, putting it on the cusp of knocking the AI chip darling off the throne as the world's most valuable company.

Nvidia has, by and large, held the crown for more than two years.

But with investors starting to question the health of the AI trade, Nvidia's Teflon stock has come under pressure. Nvidia stock is down 7.3% over the past month, while Apple stock is up 2.5%.

Apple is seen as a more defensive play, given its hardware focus.

Thursday was an absolute bloodbath for Big Tech, with the Nasdaq Composite getting slammed down nearly 2.6% in its worst single-day beatdown since June.

AI play Meta ( META ) dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results, posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012 amid aggressive spending on AI.

The company said it would issue a new tranche of stock to help fuel its AI build-out.

"With roughly 375 million iPhones that have not upgraded in over 4 years, we believe the pool of buyers waiting for a reason to upgrade is deep enough to keep Duo demand high well into 2027," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said in a note on Apple.

articles.title: American Express (AXP) Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates
articles.summary: American Express (AXP) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of +4.70% and -0.34%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 2026. Do the numbers hold...
articles.body:
American Express ( AXP ) came out with quarterly earnings of $4.68 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.47 per share. This compares to earnings of $4.14 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +4.70%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this credit card issuer and global payments company would post earnings of $4.41 per share when it actually produced earnings of $4.53, delivering a surprise of +2.72%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

American Express, which belongs to the Zacks Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry, posted revenues of $20.06 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.34%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $18.43 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

American Express shares have lost about 12.1% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12%.

While American Express has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for American Express was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

articles.title: A stronger rupee, shrinking dollar reserve: The balancing act facing RBI
articles.summary: Rupee has had a rough ride this year, sliding nearly 6% against the US dollar and hitting one record low after another.
articles.body: Rupee has had a rough ride this year, sliding nearly 6% against the US dollar and hitting one record low after another. But after coming dangerously close to the 97-per-dollar mark, the currency has clawed its way back to around 94, helped by intervention from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).Rupee had plunged to a record low of 96.96 in May and came close to breaching the 97 mark again earlier this month. It has since recovered around 2%, with the RBI stepping in to cool dollar demand.Earlier this week, rupee strengthened by 82 paise to 94.96 per dollar on the interbank order matching system, gaining nearly 0.7% from its previous closing, in a single session.As rupee continues to face a series of factors weighing it down, geopolitics, trade issues, dollar demand and more, the central bank rolled out a support system for the currency. The measures include restrictions on cancelling and rebooking foreign exchange derivative contracts, tighter documentation requirements, a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve for specified transactions and a special dollar window for public sector oil marketing companies.So, now when rupee is finally back in the seemingly safer territory, can RBI breathe easy?Not quite.The recent rebound may have given the currency some breathing room, but the apex bank still has a tricky balancing act on its hands: keeping sharp swings in check without running down its foreign exchange reserves or making it more expensive for businesses to hedge against currency risks.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The central bank also has a sizeable reserve cushion. India’s foreign exchange reserves hit a record $785.71 billion in the week ended September 4, 2026, rising by $44.9 billion in a single week, the biggest weekly increase on record. The increase was attributed to inflows through the RBI’s special dollar swap scheme, launched in June, which had brought in $136.38 billion. The record inflows coincided with the rupee rising to a two-month high.However, the size of the reserves alone does not determine how far the RBI can go in defending the currency. It must weigh the impact of intervention against India’s external payment obligations, the effect on banking liquidity and the cost of hedging currency risks.Rupee under pressure - When RBI needs to step inIn layman terms, rupee’s value depends on how many people want to buy dollars and how many are willing to sell them. So when demand for dollars rises and supply falls, rupee comes under pressure.This year, rising oil prices and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities have added to the pressure. Importers have also been buying dollars to protect themselves against a further fall in the currency, while exporters have been holding back their dollar sales.This creates a mismatch: importers need dollars to pay for goods bought abroad, but fewer dollars may be entering the market if exporters delay converting their foreign earnings into rupees. The result is greater demand for dollars, putting further pressure on the rupee.ICICI Bank, in a recent report, noted that this gap had added to dollar demand, while forward premiums had also risen in recent months.However, the RBI is not trying to keep rupee at one fixed level.Jyoti Prakash Gadia, managing director of Resurgent India Limited, told TOI that the central bank’s aim is to control sharp fluctuations in the currency, rather than defend a particular exchange rate.“There is no fixed exchange rate at which the RBI will have to act. According to the RBI’s official stance, its objective is to curb volatility rather than protect a particular level of the rupee,” the expert said.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();An orderly fall driven by differences in inflation, oil prices or the dollar’s strength in global markets may not require intervention, he added. The case for action becomes stronger when panic grips the foreign exchange market, liquidity dries up, speculative positions become destabilising or depreciation begins to fuel inflationary expectations.How is RBI trying to cool dollar demand?Earlier this month, the RBI introduced five key measures to curb excessive hedging, tighten oversight and move some dollar demand away from the regular foreign exchange market.1. Restricting cancellation and rebooking of contracts: RBI has restricted the cancellation and rebooking of foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee. Repeatedly cancelling and rebooking contracts can add to market activity. The restriction is expected to reduce such volumes, although it also makes hedging more expensive for importers.An ICICI Bank report said, “With the new measures, RBI has made it more expensive for importers to hedge. Also, the volume in the market should see a decline given cancellation and rebooking of contracts are not going to take place,”2. Cutting the limit for transactions without documentation: The threshold for certain foreign exchange derivative transactions that can be undertaken without establishing an underlying exposure has been reduced to $5 million from the earlier $100 million. The aim is to tighten oversight and curb dollar demand driven by expectations of further rupee depreciation rather than genuine business requirements.3. Tightening documentation requirements: The RBI has also tightened documentation requirements to prevent the same exposure from being hedged multiple times. This is relevant as importers seek protection against a weaker rupee while exporters hold back dollar sales, adding to the demand-supply imbalance. ICICI Bank expects the measures to bring hedging activity closer to equilibrium. Its report said, “All of these measures put together should ensure that the hedging ratio should move towards an equilibrium and thus cool off the demand for Dollars and thus the depreciation pressure on the currency,”4. Introducing a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve: The RBI introduced a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve requirement for eligible current account derivative transactions exceeding $2 million where foreign currency is purchased against the rupee. It subsequently extended the requirement to certain banks' own hedging contracts without a minimum transaction threshold. This is expected to affect liquidity alongside the RBI’s decision to increase the daily cash reserve balance requirement from 90% to 99% of the prescribed cash reserve ratio requirement. According to ICICI Bank, the two measures would sterilise around 0.4-0.6% of net demand and time liabilities (NDTL). The report also said the measures had pushed bond yields higher.5. Opening a special dollar window for oil companies: The RBI has opened a special dollar window for public sector oil marketing companies. This allows them to meet their dollar requirements through the facility, taking their demand out of the regular foreign exchange market in the immediate term. Together, the measures are intended to ease pressure on dollar demand. However, ICICI Bank has cautioned that sustained currency stability will depend on broader external conditions, particularly capital flows and crude oil prices.Stronger buffer, but how much can the RBI spend?Foreign exchange reserves give the RBI a cushion to manage sharp falls in rupee. When the central bank sells dollars in the market, banks pay for them in rupees. This adds to the supply of dollars and can help ease pressure on the currency.India’s foreign exchange reserves hit a record $785.71 billion in the week ended September 4, 2026, after rising by a record $44.9 billion in a single week. However, RBI data showed that reserves had fallen to around $726 billion as of October 9, 2026.So, how much can the RBI afford to spend to support the rupee? There is no fixed limit, said Jyoti Prakash Gadia, managing director of Resurgent India Limited. The key is whether the reserves are enough to meet the country’s needs.“The RBI does not have any fixed specific amount of money that it can spend in defending the value of the Indian rupee. The issue lies in how much reserves will be sufficient in comparison to the volume of India’s total annual imports, repayment obligations of its external debt, possible future outflows of capital and other forward obligations. According to the data of the RBI, as of October 9, 2026, the level of reserves is close to $726 billion,” the expert told TOI.However, he added that the headline reserve figure alone does not show how much the RBI can comfortably spend. The bigger concern is whether the central bank is using up reserves without restoring market confidence.A stronger rupee alongside falling reserves can be a warning sign, too. “An appreciation of the rupee along with decreasing foreign reserves suggests that intervention is acting as a buffer to external pressures instead of an improvement in the dollar situation,” Gadia said.Selling dollars can help limit the short-term rise in the cost of imports and ease inflationary pressure. But if the RBI has to keep using its reserves to support the rupee without improving market confidence, the strategy becomes harder to sustain.Gadia also cautioned that a weekly fall in reserves does not necessarily mean the RBI has sold dollars, as changes in valuation can also affect the total.To assess how comfortably India can manage external pressure, it is therefore important to look beyond the headline reserve figure. Import cover, external debt repayments, capital flows, forward contracts and the reserves actually available for use all matter.The cost of intervention: Costlier hedging and tighter liquidityThe RBI’s curbs have unsettled parts of the currency market where businesses hedge exchange-rate risks and banks manage their exposures.According to anonymous bankers cited by Reuters, rupee forward premiums rose to multi-year highs earlier this week after the latest foreign exchange curbs tightened liquidity and made it harder for traders to manage exposures.The one-year implied hedging cost rose by more than 90 basis points during the week to 4.6%, its highest level since January 2022. This was well above the roughly 2% implied by the India-US interest-rate differential.The strain was sharper for shorter tenors. The three-month implied hedging cost rose to 7.2%, against a theoretical 1.5%. Overnight swap costs climbed to around two paise, more than four times their usual levels, partly driven by the RBI’s sell/buy swaps.The report also noted that the gap between onshore and non-deliverable forward rupee rates had widened. The one-month deliverable dollar-rupee forward premium was last quoted at around 60 paise, compared with 50 paise offshore. Bankers said bid-ask spreads on one-year forward premiums had widened significantly.These figures reflect the strain reported by market participants. Hedging helps businesses manage uncertainty over future currency payments, but a rise in hedging costs makes protection against rupee depreciation more expensive.Intervention also affects liquidity in the banking system. Gadia explained that when the RBI sells dollars in the spot market, banks use rupees to buy them, reducing their balances with the central bank and draining liquidity.The impact depends on the amount of liquidity already available.In Gadia’s words, “In a tight liquidity system, persistent offloading could cause the overnight rates to rise due to increased costs of borrowing and perhaps even lead to the rates of borrowing and bonds increasing. On the other hand, in a liquidity surplus system, the offload could just end up removing the excess liquidity.”The RBI can offset the drain through repurchase transactions or by purchasing government bonds to replenish cash in the market, he added.The trade-off is that efforts to ease currency pressure can affect liquidity, borrowing costs and the price businesses pay to manage foreign exchange exposure.At the same time, a weaker rupee does not affect every group in the same way. Intervention to support the currency also creates winners and losers.According to Gadia, importers benefit when RBI dollar sales help the rupee appreciate to a level stronger than it would otherwise have reached. Companies with unhedged dollar liabilities can also gain, while consumers may benefit indirectly if imported inflation eases. However, the impact on consumer prices is neither immediate nor complete.Exporters and people receiving remittances from abroad, on the other hand, get fewer rupees for their dollars than they would have received if the rupee had depreciated further. Cheaper imported inputs can partly offset this disadvantage for exporters. Investors leaving India may also receive additional dollars in return for their rupees when the currency is stronger than it would otherwise have been.If not RBI, who rescues rupee?If the RBI reduces intervention, Gadia said, rupee is likely to depreciate further until demand and supply move towards equilibrium. That could raise import costs, inflation and the cost of servicing unhedged foreign exchange debt, while making exports more competitive.However, depreciation alone does not guarantee an export boost. The benefit depends on demand in foreign markets, manufacturing capabilities and the cost of imported raw materials.“If RBI intervention is reduced, the Indian rupee is likely to depreciate further until supply and demand for the rupee come to an equilibrium. This could result in increased cost of imports, inflation, and unhedged foreign exchange debts while making exports more competitive. The extent to which exports benefit from rupee depreciation depends on foreign market demand, manufacturing capabilities, and the cost of imported raw materials.”Gadia also identified several possible strategies: intervention aimed at correcting disorderly markets, inflation management, policies that encourage long-term capital inflows and improved corporate hedging. Raising interest rates may be useful when justified by inflation considerations, but it would also slow economic growth.The debate has drawn differing views from policymakers and economists.The International Monetary Fund said India should allow the exchange rate to move as the first line of defence. Economists, meanwhile, have warned that exchange rates can overshoot during global disruptions and should not automatically be treated as stabilisers.Michael Debabrata Patra, former deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) told Reuters that effective communication could help cushion the impact of global disruptions.“What could possibly help in promoting orderly market activity and bolstering market confidence is perhaps timely and patient communication to shape expectations,” he told Reuters.The supplied report also noted that the RBI’s monetary policy committee had raised the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points at its most recent meeting and changed its stance from “neutral” to “calibrated tightening”.The minutes reflected caution about tightening too quickly and inhibiting economic growth.Possible strategies include intervention aimed at correcting disorderly markets, inflation management, policies that promote long-term capital inflows, and improved corporate hedging. Raising interest rates might be useful where such a strategy is warranted by inflation considerations but will slow economic growth.The bottom lineA stronger rupee alongside falling foreign exchange reserves may suggest that the RBI is cushioning the currency against external pressures rather than easing those pressures. While selling dollars can help limit the rise in import costs in the short term, repeatedly using reserves to support rupee can become a concern if market confidence does not improve. Gadia also cautioned that weekly declines in reserves may partly reflect changes in valuation.The RBI’s challenge, therefore, is not simply to push rupee higher. It is to curb sharp fluctuations while keeping enough reserves to meet India’s import needs, repay external debt and deal with possible future capital outflows.The recent recovery shows that measures to curb dollar demand can help ease pressure on the currency. But higher hedging costs, liquidity concerns and the risk of further external shocks show that intervention comes with its own costs. As ICICI Bank noted, lasting stability will also depend on capital flows and crude oil prices.Ultimately, the RBI must weigh how much intervention can achieve against what it costs. The aim is not to defend a particular number on the exchange-rate screen at any price, but to keep the market orderly without leaving the economy with a thinner safety net.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russian diesel tanker heads to the U.S., the first since Trump’s deal with Putin
articles.summary: A tanker loaded with diesel fuel set sail Friday from Russia for the United States, the first shipment since President Donald Trump agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into the global market.
articles.body: A tanker loaded with diesel fuel set sail Friday from Russia for the United States, the first shipment since President Donald Trump agreed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release more fuel into the global market. Trump eased some sanctions on the Kremlin two weeks ago and has since waived more, reversing years of American policy despite Moscow’s ongoing illegal invasion of Ukraine in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the Midterm elections. The ship’s departure for the U.S. was confirmed by the Kremlin. The tanker, a Malta-flagged shipped named “Agioi Fanendes,” left a port in Russia’s Primorsk today, according to MarineTraffic tracking data reviewed by NBC News. The ship listed New York as its destination. Energy Aspects, a market intelligence firm, said that it had confirmed with its industry sources that the ship loaded up 298,000 barrels of diesel in Primorsk. The firm said that currently the ship plans to unload that fuel in New York. It is expected to arrive on Tuesday, November 10. The ship’s expected arrival would put it just after the midterm elections. Trump’s Republican party is on edge for potentially heavy losses in House and Senate seats its candidates are defending, driven in part by blowback from consumers facing soaring energy prices. Trump and his administration have scrambled to try to bring down those prices, which have increased in the wake of supply shocks stemming from the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars. Trump has taken a number of steps to warm ties with the Kremlin and pressure Kyiv to agree to end the war, drawing outrage from Ukraine and its bipartisan backers in Congress. “I believe there have already been reports from the Ministry of Energy that the first tanker has departed for its destinations and that further shipments will continue on a regular basis,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said early Friday. Crude oil was headed for a third straight weekly gain. Brent, the most important global oil benchmark, traded around $114 per barrel, less than $13 away from its highest point this year. Since the start of the year, the average price of diesel fuel has soared from $3.55 per gallon to $6.32, an unprecedented rise of 78%. Energy Aspect’s analysts said the impact of the cargo’s arrival would likely be “limited.” Diesel’s sky-high price has troubled economists more than the jump in the price of regular gasoline because, “the cost of diesel gets into just about everything,” as KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk told NBC News in an August interview. “Everything from … running a farm … cost of food, but also everything across the economy that’s shipped gets that extra fee tacked onto it,” she said. Currently, U.S. daily diesel demand is about 3.8M barrels per day, meaning that Friday’s shipment would satisfy not even a full day’s worth of usage. “Global distillate markets have tightened sharply,” said Bank of America’s head of global commodities Francisco Blanch in a recent note, adding that it signals “an acute scarcity of refined products.” Diesel is a distillate fuel, produced by refining crude oil. “Geopolitical disruptions are exacerbating that shortage as attacks on shipping around Hormuz make energy flows more difficult and costly, while attacks on Russian refining capacity further restrict product availability,” he wrote. Russia has historically been one of the world’s largest exporters of diesel. In September and for some of October, the Kremlin restricted the export of diesel fuel amid a Ukrainian campaign of attacks on its energy infrastructure. It lifted those export restrictions after Putin’s diesel deal with Trump. Easing sanctions on Russia to open up some previously-blocked diesel supplies was just the latest in a number of policy levers pulled by Trump. In just the last few weeks, the president has also signed an order allowing more widespread use of an off-road variety of diesel. The administration also pressured European allies, particularly Germany and France, to urgently release some of their diesel reserves. The administration has also reportedly pushed for a fresh release of crude and diesel reserves, though the International Energy Agency has rebuffed that request. Experts say that even all together, Trump’s actions will do little to help ease prices which have continued to trend higher. “Policy intervention can provide temporary relief, but there is no silver bullet for diesel,” Blanch wrote.

articles.title: GM Analysts Say Buy the Dip as Stock Eyes Worst Week Since 2025
articles.summary: General Motors Co. stock is set to record its worst week in more than 20 months, but bullish Wall Street analysts are doubling down.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- General Motors Co. stock is set to record its worst week in more than 20 months, but bullish Wall Street analysts are doubling down.

The carmaker's stock has fallen 8% through Thursday's close, putting it on pace for the largest weekly drop since January 2025, and analysts are saying investors should buy the dip.

On Tuesday, the company narrowed the top- and bottom-ends of this year's profit guidance range, and its Chief Executive Officer Mary Barra warned that GM faces "clear external headwinds," sending the stock down 6.8% in the worst session since July 2025.

"The bar was high," said StoneX analyst Mickey Legg. "It's a buying opportunity. Most of what spooked the market is timing rather than earnings power."

StoneX's Legg, who has a buy rating on GM, is not alone in his call. None of the analysts tracked by Bloomberg recommend selling the stock after Wells Fargo dropped coverage of the company amid an analyst departure last month. Still, GM shares are down year-to-date, declining 5.1% as the S&P 500 climbed 12%.

Analysts at BNP Paribas, Evercore ISI, and RBC Capital Markets echoed the call to buy the dip after Tuesday's earnings. BNP's James Picariello reiterated his buy-equivalent rating, citing GM's "severely discounted valuation" and unparalleled execution.

When GM last reported earnings in July, quarterly profit beat and management hiked its outlook. Shares rallied over the next few days to touch a record high.

But the stock has retreated since amid lofty oil and high costs, elevated interest rates, and weak consumer sentiment.

"The market has focused excessively on these near-term headwinds while overlooking the company's improving operating performance, margins, and cash generation." said Ivan Feinseth, chief investment officer at Tigress Financial Partners.

articles.title: Kalshi Courts Wall Street in Bid to Be the ‘Inflation Exchange’
articles.summary: Kalshi Inc. is opening up a new frontier in its rivalry with traditional financial exchanges by pitching the world’s largest banks and hedge funds on a futur...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Kalshi Inc. is opening up a new frontier in its rivalry with traditional financial exchanges by pitching the world's largest banks and hedge funds on a futures market tied to US inflation.

The New York-based firm, best known for its prediction markets, is targeting a December launch for exchange-traded futures contracts tracking both the consumer price index and the closely watched core gauge of inflation, which excludes food and energy, according to people familiar with the matter. The firm has tapped Michael Ashton, a former Barclays Plc trader known as the "Inflation Guy," to design the contracts and drum up interest with big investment firms.

The contracts would be the only futures tied directly to CPI, giving Kalshi a unique way to court macro investors active in the multi-trillion-dollar markets for interest-rate and bond futures that are currently offered by CME Group Inc. and Intercontinental Exchange Inc. CME tried to roll out CPI futures in the past but does not currently offer them.

Kalshi is looking to roll out the product at a time when inflation has become a central preoccupation for trading desks trying to get ahead of potential rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

"There's no exchange that trades this and they want to be the inflation exchange," said Ashton, the managing principal of Enduring Investments LLC.

A Kalshi spokesperson confirmed they were working on CPI futures, but declined to provide details on the rollout.

The CPI futures are the latest in a dizzying array of new financial products rolled out by Kalshi and a handful of other startup exchanges.

Kalshi's prediction market exchange is dominated by sports betting, but it already offers event contracts that allow customers to bet on whether CPI comes in above or below a certain level each month. Those binary contracts, though, have primarily been attractive to retail investors because they don't offer the kind of smooth payout outcomes that institutional investors and traders are typically seeking.

Kalshi also has a growing business in so-called perpetual contracts, or perps, tracking the likes of crypto tokens and commodities. Unlike the new CPI futures, though, perps do not have any expiration date, which make it hard for them to slot into the existing Wall Street financial infrastructure. The CPI futures give Kalshi a new kind of product and a way to test expanding into traditional futures markets.

Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran , marking the oil giant's first such evacuation since the Iran war began.

This week, the New York Times reported that the US and Israel have reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the midterm elections next month, raising expectations of increased fighting in the region.

The US has ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia after a series of attacks at the country's airports and oil fields .

President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will fall afterward.

On Friday, the national price of gasoline stood at $4.29 per gallon, roughly $1.22 higher than a year ago. Diesel hovered around $6.31, about $2.68 more than this time last year.

A power outage at a refinery in the Chicago area is expected to send refined fuel prices even higher in the region.

articles.title: SK Hynix pulls a $150 billion IPO as its own record US listing sits underwater
articles.summary: SK Hynix raised a record $26.5 billion in its US debut in July. Now it's pulling a $150 billion IPO.
articles.body:
In July, SK Hynix ( SKHY ) raised $26.5 billion in the biggest US listing ever by a foreign company. Now the company is walking away from one of the biggest tech IPOs ever.

The South Korean memory giant said Friday it has shelved plans to list Solidigm, its flash memory unit, in the US, citing market conditions and share price trends. Solidigm had aimed to raise $10 billion to $15 billion at a valuation of up to $150 billion, according to industry estimates cited by the Wall Street Journal .

For a clue to why, look at the company's own stock.

SK Hynix priced its US shares at $149 in July. SK Hynix stock is rising on Friday but still trades below that price, about a third below the stock's September record.

Memory and storage stocks have shed $1.3 trillion in market value from their 2026 records, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. SK Hynix accounts for about $489 billion of that, and Micron ( MU ) accounts for about $411 billion. Of the 59 chip stocks in a Yahoo Finance basket, 58 are down in October.

That's a strange look for an industry printing money. Memory makers are booking record profits on AI data center demand, and executives see shortages lasting into 2028. The stocks are trading as if the peak is already in, after a $3 trillion chip rout this month.

Solidigm isn't the only AI-linked deal getting pulled back. Australian data center operator Firmus Grid canceled its IPO, and AirTrunk delayed its Singapore listing to next year. OpenAI is now seeking a $1.25 trillion valuation in funding talks , down from $1.4 trillion. Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) blockbuster IPO is expected next month.

The next test for memory stocks comes on Thursday, when Sandisk ( SNDK ) reports after the close.

For SK Hynix, watch $149. A move back above its IPO price would put July's buyers back in the black. Until then, it's a ceiling.

articles.title: US Business Activity Expands, Prices Surge by Most Since 2022
articles.summary: US business activity grew at a slightly slower pace in October but remained close to a multi-year high as robust demand pushed new orders, employment and pri...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- US business activity grew at a slightly slower pace in October but remained close to a multi-year high as robust demand pushed new orders, employment and prices higher.

The S&P Global flash composite index fell 0.8 point to 57.6 in October, data released Friday showed. That was the second-highest reading since 2022. Figures above 50 indicate expansion.

A gauge of selling prices rose at the fastest pace in more than four years, reflecting a sharp rise in the cost of energy, transportation and raw materials.

"Cost pressures remain a key concern, notably as the renewed surge in oil prices reverberates through to impact a wide variety of goods and services," Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said in a statement.

Bottlenecks are also getting worse. Supplier delivery times lengthened the most since 2022, with S&P Global citing material and labor shortages as well as overloaded suppliers and shipping delays.

Even so, Williamson said that, outside the pandemic reopening, US businesses are enjoying their strongest period of growth since 2015.

Strong consumer spending, AI-fueled investment and defense outlays have all bolstered US businesses this year. New orders, a gauge of demand, posted the fastest growth in four-and-a-half years in October.

Firms are responding by adding more workers. The composite index for employment was the second-highest in four years, and the manufacturing index showed factory headcount advancing at the fastest pace since 2012.

Looking ahead, investment in artificial intelligence and related technologies is anticipated to support demand and the broader economy next year, too. Forecasters raised their estimates for private investment growth in the third quarter and across all of 2027 in the latest Bloomberg News survey of economists.

The group's overall manufacturing index inched up to 56, the strongest since May 2022, while a gauge of activity at service providers eased.

articles.summary: Salta para analizar una propuesta de rebaja del IRPF planteada por José María Figaredo, portavoz de Economía de Vox, respecto a impuestos y prestaciones públicas
articles.body: Las prestaciones son otro tema de debate muy abierto en España. Ha sido el economista Gonzalo Bernardos el que ha entrado en el asunto para analizar una propuesta de rebaja del IRPF planteada por José María Figaredo, portavoz de Economía de Vox, respecto a impuestos y prestaciones públicas. Y lanzó el órdago. "En España, el 80% de los ciudadanos cobra más en prestaciones, de forma directa o indirecta, que lo que paga en impuestos”, sentenció. Es más, mostró su objeción a la propuesta fiscal en el reparto del ahorro y en sus consecuencias para financiar servicios públicos: “El que más beneficiado está es el que más gana”, indicó. FEDEA lleva a cabo un estudio sobre el reparto de los impuestos y las prestaciones entre los hogares españoles donde se incluye pensiones, desempleo y ayudas económicas, más el valor de la sanidad y la educación públicas. Los tres grupos que reúnen al 60% de los hogares con menor renta eran, de media, beneficiarios netos en 2023, mientras que los dos superiores aportaban más de lo que recibían. Son promedios: dentro de cada tramo conviven situaciones diferentes. En conjunto, los impuestos y las prestaciones analizados redujeron la desigualdad un 31,9%, con las pensiones como principal elemento redistributivo entre las ayudas monetarias. Por todo ello, Bernardos ha abordado esa cuestión en varias ocasiones: “Gracias a pagar impuestos tenemos un ascensor social y personas sin recursos pueden llegar a la universidad”. Y es que la educación permite entender por qué el balance familiar va más allá del dinero ingresado en una cuenta. Porque el acceso a las aulas y a la formación universitaria también forma parte de los recursos financiados colectivamente.

articles.title: Amex to Cut 5% of Headcount Globally as Cost Pressures Mount
articles.summary: American Express Co. is cutting 5% of its headcount globally as Chief Executive Officer Steve Squeri seeks to keep a lid on the company’s rising costs.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- American Express Co. is cutting 5% of its headcount globally as Chief Executive Officer Steve Squeri seeks to keep a lid on the company's rising costs.

Squeri told Bloomberg TV that the company has 78,000 employees, meaning the move will affect about 3,500 jobs.

Financial firms have been cutting jobs in recent months, with some companies attributing the changes to the increased use of artificial intelligence. This week, Barclays Plc said it would eliminate 5,000 jobs. HSBC Holdings Plc is planning job reductions across its UK wealth-management business, Bloomberg News reported earlier this month, and Citigroup Inc. has also been lowering its headcount.

Squeri said on a call with analysts Friday that the job cuts reflect the desire to make the company more agile and efficient, and find ways to reduce layers and speed up decision making.

The company has also been facing consistent pressure to keep and retain its premium card members. To do that, Amex has been refreshing certain cards, adding a raft of new perks last year to its Platinum card. Earlier this month, the company said it would work with Airbnb Inc. to allow for certain luxury rentals on its travel site to count for the cardholders' annual lodging credit.

Overall, that's boosted costs. The New York-based firm said expenses climbed about 9% to $14.5 billion in the third quarter, although it was less than the $14.8 billion estimate from analysts.

Costs for member rewards were up 10% in the quarter, while marketing expenses rose 11%. Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec had previously said to expect marketing expenses to increase by around 10% in the second half of 2026 compared with last year.

"It's been highly competitive," Squeri said about the fight for premium cardholders on the call. "And our assumption is that it will remain highly competitive."

Amex shares were down 1.8% to $319.45 at 9:35 a.m. in New York trading Friday, extending this year's drop to nearly 14%.

The workforce cuts were announced after Amex posted third-quarter earnings that beat estimates, with adjusted earnings per share of $4.68 surpassing the $4.49 average analyst estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

articles.title: Apple's iPhone Duo hits stores today with limited supplies and long lines
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo goes on sale Friday, but in-store supplies will be limited.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone Duo goes on sale today, but limited supplies and long lines outside Apple Stores mean you'll have to be lucky to get your hands on one.

Preorders for the company's first foldable smartphone sold out almost immediately last week, with delivery times currently pushed out well into late January.

Apple said it planned to have some Duos available in stores but expects them to sell out quickly.

"On Friday morning, our teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a statement earlier this week.

"Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we're working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible."

At least some of the preorder madness comes down to scalpers hawking the foldable iPhone on sites like eBay at a stiff markup.

While the iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, sellers are asking for upwards of $4,000 for the base model. At least one seller is offering a Duo with 2TB of storage, which Apple sells for $3,199, for a staggering $15,000.

The Duo is one of Apple's most anticipated products in years. The biggest update to the company's most important device since it launched in 2007, the iPhone Duo could help raise the iPhone's average selling price, boosting Apple's bottom line.

The iPhone represented $209.58 billion of Apple's $416.16 billion in total revenue in 2025. That's well ahead of the company's second-largest business segment, Services, which brought in $109.15 billion.

The Duo also comes as Apple revamps its iPhone release schedule. Rather than debuting its full lineup of phones at its annual September event last month, Apple revealed only its top-tier smartphones, including the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.

The company is widely expected to unveil its standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 early next year. That should help even out the lumpiness in Apple's seasonal sales and provide a clearer picture of which devices consumers are purchasing.

articles.title: Etsy to restrict AI-generated content in effort to combat seller slop
articles.summary: Etsy announced new restrictions on AI-generated content on its platform, saying it threatens the integrity of sellers’ work and leaves buyers exposed to fraud.
articles.body: Etsy announced new restrictions Thursday on AI-generated content on its platform, saying it threatens the integrity of its sellers’ work and leaves buyers exposed to fraud. Among the new stipulations: Patterns, recipes, or any other item that involves a buyer “putting in effort to achieve a finished product” cannot be created using AI.Sellers must include at least one unaltered photo of the actual item against a real background.Bot-generated listings are banned. AI-generated art can still be sold on the platform as long as merchants “Play a clear role in what they create and are transparent about the process,” Etsy said in a note to sellers. “Our marketplace only works when buyers and sellers trust each other,” Etsy Vice President of Customer Operations James Ossman wrote in a blog post. “Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it. We know we have work to do to uphold this standard on Etsy.” Etsy hosts more than 5 million entrepreneurs, most of whom are women who run one-person businesses out of their homes, according to an annual company report. That distinguishes it from other major e-commerce platforms like Amazon and eBay, though it commands a fraction of those platforms’ revenues. As of 2024, Etsy hosted $10.9 billion-worth of goods’ sales, compared with about $75 billion for eBay and more than $700 billion for Amazon. Some buyers responded positively to Etsy’s announcement. “I can’t explain how infuriating it has been to purchase a crochet pattern, only to open the PDF and realize it’s fully AI-generated, doesn’t make sense, and definitely doesn’t match what the finished product should be,” creator Kara Lynne said on X. The dawn of advanced AI has led to an explosion in AI-generated sales content — and a growing backlash from consumers against what they see as AI slop. A recent social media trend among cafes and restaurants saw owners pledging not to use AI after egregious examples of AI-generated food images in the wild were shared on social media. Major platforms are responding to the growing discontent. Many, including Facebook and Instagram, now work to append labels to images or videos created via AI. Others, like LinkedIn, have added buttons allowing users to report AI-generated content. Snap has banned wholly AI-generated content from its recommendation algorithm, while Spotify recently announced it had removed 50 million AI-generated tracks from its platform. Ossman said Etsy would add a function similar to LinkedIn’s that makes it easier for users to report listings that include misleading AI imagery. He also said Etsy would be using technology to identify misleading imagery and fraudulent listings, with the goal of expanding removals of illicit listings in the coming months. “We’re actively working to address the questions AI raises for our marketplace,” Ossman said in the post. “This work is hard, and we don’t have every answer today. But I believe this is an important moment for Etsy, and that these initial steps are putting us on the right path.”

articles.title: India’s Scotch whisky row as firms seek 75% duty instead of 150%
articles.summary: India’s investigation into Scotch whisky imports by Diageo and Pernod Ricard has sparked a dispute over the India–UK trade deal, which cut import duties
articles.body: India’s investigation into Scotch whisky imports by Diageo and Pernod Ricard has sparked a dispute over the India–UK trade deal, which cut import duties on eligible Scotch whisky from 150 percent to 75 percent, with a further reduction to 40 percent planned over the next 10 years.According to Reuters, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India (ISWAI), which represents the two companies, has written to the commerce minister seeking urgent intervention, warning that India’s interpretation of customs rules could prevent bulk Scotch concentrates imported from Britain from benefiting from the reduced duty.The dispute centres on whether bulk Scotch concentrates imported from Britain qualify for the lower tariff under the trade agreement. Indian revenue investigators have maintained that the concentrates should attract the full 150 percent import duty, rather than the reduced 75 percent rate available to eligible Scotch whisky products.The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) searched the offices of Diageo and Pernod Ricard this month and questioned executives as part of an investigation into whether the companies misclassified imports to benefit from lower duties. The investigation is ongoing, and the allegations have not been established as wrongdoing.The industry group has warned that the interpretation could undermine a key benefit negotiated under the India–UK agreement. The tariff reduction was intended to improve market access for British products, including Scotch whisky, but the dispute has raised questions over which imported products qualify for the concession.Diageo and Pernod Ricard import bulk Scotch concentrates from Britain and blend them with other ingredients to manufacture popular Indian-market brands, including Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s. The outcome of the investigation could affect the companies’ import costs and the commercial benefits they expected from the trade deal.The dispute has implications for India’s alcohol industry, valued at around $65 billion. Britain accounts for almost 75 percent of India’s imported spirits, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, according to Crisil Ratings.ISWAI has called for urgent clarification from the government to ensure that the tariff benefits agreed under the trade deal can be implemented as intended. articles.title: Infosys ADRs tumble 6% as FY27 growth guidance cut to 1%-2%
articles.summary: Infosys ADRs drop 6% after cutting FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1%-2%; North America weak, high-tech and retail slump, AI revenue rises.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Infosys had a lacklustre Q2, with its shares falling 6% in early trade on the NYSE after it cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% in constant currency terms from 1.5%-3% earlier. This is the company’s weakest growth outlook in seven years, reflecting subdued volumes, pricing pressure and weakness in its mainstay market, North America, where revenue declined 1.5% year on year.The slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7%, respectively, in constant currency terms.Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries. “We have seen different client-specific situations in both retail and high-tech. This is not happening across all industries. We continue to see strong growth and discretionary spending in financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing,” he said.CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka said volumes remained subdued, while competitive intensity and clients’ higher productivity expectations had put pressure on pricing. Discretionary spending in retail and high-tech was also lower than anticipated, he said, adding that these factors had led to the guidance cut.Retail was additionally affected by a larger third-party component in the previous quarters, creating an unfavourable sequential comparison. While weakness in high-tech and retail was broadly similar across geographies, the impact was more pronounced in the US, Sanghrajka said. The company retained its operating margin guidance at 20%-22% for FY27.In dollar terms, Infosys’ revenue rose 1.2% sequentially and 1.3% year on year to $5.1 billion in the September quarter. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.2% sequentially and 1.5% year on year.AI was a bright spot, accounting for 10.5% of revenue and growing 29% sequentially, compared with 8.2% in the previous quarter, Parekh said. Operating margin remained flat sequentially at 21%. Post-sales customer support costs had a 70-basis-point impact, reflecting a reversal in the previous quarter followed by an expense this quarter. Acquisitions added a further 20-basis-point impact due to an extra month of amortisation.Large deals totalled $5.2 billion during the quarter, including two mega deals. One was a new seven-year contract worth more than $2 billion with a large international company, which is expected to contribute over one percentage point to revenue growth in FY28. The other was a $1 billion renewal.“Our deal pipeline remains healthy and includes other potential mega deals,” Parekh said.However, AI-driven productivity gains are also putting pressure on traditional services revenue, while competition remains intense. Parekh said Infosys would take on contracts only when they met its economic criteria. articles.title: U.S. airlines favor higher fares over fuller planes as fuel costs squeeze profits
articles.summary: U.S. airlines are increasingly willing to fly with empty seats rather than slash fares simply to fill ​them, at a time of soaring fuel costs.
articles.body: U.S. airlines are increasingly willing to fly with empty seats rather than slash fares simply to fill ​them, betting that disciplined pricing and flight schedules will help protect profits at a time of soaring fuel costs. The strategy has delivered substantial revenue gains as demand has ‌held up despite sharp fare increases. Yet profits have still been squeezed as jet fuel prices surged roughly 90% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February, forcing several major carriers to cut earnings forecasts. Executives at Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, American Airlines, Southwest Airlines and Alaska Air Group have emphasized protecting margins over boosting passenger volumes. Their resolve faces a test in 2027. Industry schedules point to more flying capacity, potentially intensifying competition for passengers even as fuel ​prices are expected to stay high and making this year’s substantial fare gains harder to repeat. “If fuel stays elevated, we have to continue to push yield up so that ​we can make a bit of money,” American Chief Financial Officer Devon May told Reuters on Thursday. Yield is the revenue airlines collect for each ⁠mile passengers fly. Six major U.S. airlines plan to grow domestic capacity 3.0% in the fourth quarter from a year earlier and 3.8% in the first quarter of 2027, a sharp acceleration from just ​0.2% growth in the third quarter, according to Airlines for America, citing Cirium data. U.S. air fares rose an average of nearly 23% year-on-year in the seven months through September, far outpacing the 3.6% average ​increase in overall consumer prices, according to Labor Department data. Airlines are still seeking increases. JetBlue Airways initiated a $10 one-way increase in domestic published fares on Wednesday, JP Morgan said, following a similar United-led increase the previous week that Southwest subsequently matched. United said it had nothing further to add, while Southwest said it does not publicly discuss pricing. JetBlue did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A different approach Airlines have long balanced fares against how full their ​planes are. But elevated fuel costs have made executives more willing to sacrifice occupancy and avoid discounts. United’s commercial chief Andrew Nocella offered an example during Wednesday’s earnings call. Its leisure load factor, ​a measure of how many available seats are occupied, fell 1.3 percentage points in the third quarter. Nocella acknowledged that the decline showed “a small amount of elasticity given higher ticket prices,” but called it “a trade we would make ‌every day.” American ⁠Airlines planes flew less full in the third quarter even as passenger yields jumped more than 18%. Finance chief May told Reuters the trade was deliberate. Delta has also been “managing the business for margins,” CEO Ed Bastian said. Across Delta, United, American, Southwest and Alaska, passenger revenue rose nearly $8.8 billion, or 18%, in the third quarter from a year earlier, while passenger traffic increased less than 1%. The divergence shows how much revenue growth now depends on earning more from each passenger rather than carrying more of them. Premium products and changes in passenger mix have also contributed to the gains. The Transportation Security Administration ​screened 2.9% fewer people at U.S. airports in ​the quarter than a year earlier, raising questions ⁠about whether higher fares are beginning to discourage travel. Limited capacity growth and the shutdown of budget carrier Spirit Airlines have also weighed on traffic. Airline executives insisted that demand remains resilient. “Those higher fares are not causing an erosion of volumes,” Southwest CEO Bob Jordan told analysts, after the airline ​reported a nearly 22% increase in average passenger fares in the first nine months of this year. The 2027 test But record revenues have not been ​enough to shield profits from ⁠soaring fuel costs. Gulf Coast spot jet fuel prices have risen from $2.43 a gallon before the war began in February to $4.63 on October 20, according to U.S. Energy Information Administration data. Delta and Southwest have cut their annual earnings forecasts, while American expects a full-year loss despite sharply higher passenger revenue. Airlines are now scrutinizing expansion plans. American intends to slow growth considerably next year, with May saying the carrier was reassessing whether additional flights ⁠would generate enough ​revenue to cover their operating costs. Southwest has pledged not to pursue growth at the expense of profitability, while United ​executives have cautioned that airlines’ published 2027 capacity plans may not materialize. Such restraint could help maintain higher fares. But flying less can raise operating costs per seat, while pushing prices higher risks discouraging travelers who have already absorbed steep increases. But airline ​executives say a disciplined approach on capacity can allow the industry to hold on to pricing gains. “We think these yield gains are very sustainable,” May said.

articles.title: Oil on fire, Goa, Tamil Nadu cut VAT on jet fuel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid surging crude prices, two key states on Friday finally relented by cutting VAT on aviation turbine fuel (ATF).
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid surging crude prices, two key states on Friday finally relented by cutting VAT on aviation turbine fuel (ATF). Tamil Nadu reduced the rate from 29% TO 16% at Chennai; and to 1% at all other airports in the state. Similarly, Goa has reduced VAT from 15% to 7%. Most other states had much earlier cut taxes on jet fuel as the same has been rising relentlessly since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb.Tamil Nadu industries minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana said on X Friday: “We are reducing VAT on aviation fuel for domestic airlines from 29% to 16% at Chennai Airport, and to just 1% at other airports across Tamil Nadu. By slashing this, we are taking a decisive step towards making air travel more accessible and our regional airports more competitive. Lower operating costs can encourage airlines to introduce new routes, increase flight frequencies and expand operations beyond Chennai… we are building an aviation ecosystem that connects more regions, unlocks economic potential and powers Tamil Nadu’s next phase of growth.”Thanking Goa on X Friday, IndiGo said on X: “We sincerely thank Goa CM Pramod P Sawant for the progressive decision to rationalise VAT on ATF in the state. This is a welcome move towards strengthening the aviation ecosystem, enhancing air connectivity and supporting Goa’s vibrant tourism sector. We hope this progressive approach inspires others to consider similar measures, particularly at a time when ATF costs remain high, to help make air travel more accessible for customers. Thank you for your continued commitment to fostering growth and progress in aviation.”Airlines globally are finding it tough to remain airborne due to twin pressures of ATF price hikes and airspace closures. For Indian carriers, two other factors further aggravate the situation — rupee weakening with most costs like lease rentals and maintenance being dollar-denominated and closure of Pakistan airspace which has made the flights to and from west longer for them.The Federation of Indian Airlines (FIA), that has Air India, IndiGo and SpiceJet as members, had earlier this month warned govt they will be forced to cut flights on “unviable routes” as aviation turbine fuel prices are now at the highest level in a decade.“Fuel component historically constituted about 30% to 40% of airline operating costs. (It) has increased to about 55% to 60% under the prevailing circumstances. In addition, airspace restrictions have resulted in longer flight routes, leading to higher fuel consumption, increased crew costs, and lower aircraft utilisation. Airlines are also facing additional pressure from depreciation of the Indian rupee, as key expenses such as fuel, aircraft leases, maintenance, and insurance are US dollar denominated,” says a recent FIA SOS sent to the Union aviation ministry.FIA has urged an “urgent support to continue uninterrupted operations and provide air connectivity during these challenging periods.” It had sought ATF pricing on cost plus model; ATF excise duty relief; Key states to reduce VAT on ATF and extend concession on landing and parking charges. “Such measures would provide much-needed support to the aviation sector, help preserve affordable air travel for passengers, and enable airlines to continue contributing to India's economic growth and connectivity objectives despite the challenging operating environment. If timely relief is not available, the airlines may be compelled to withdraw from several unsustainable routes,” FIA letter says.The industry says the “unprecedented financial and operational challenges” “have severely strained airline liquidity and working capital, necessitating immediate got support.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Consumer confidence holds steady from September amid persistent inflation
articles.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment flatlined from September to October, as persistent inflation squeezes Americans’ finances. Consumer confidence sat at a measure of 48 percent this month, a minor decrease from last month’s reading of 48.1, according to the University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers Index. Consumer sentiment has dipped by 10.4 percent from October 2025, with…
articles.body:
U.S. consumer sentiment flatlined from September to October, as persistent inflation squeezes Americans’ finances.

Consumer confidence sat at a measure of 48 percent this month, a minor decrease from last month’s reading of 48.1, according to the University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers Index .

Consumer sentiment has dipped by 10.4 percent from October 2025, with sentiment regarding present economic conditions declining by 20.3 percent during that time period — from 58.6 percent a year ago to 46.7 this month, per the index.

Annual inflation, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), ticked up from 3.4 percent in August to 3.7 percent in September .

Energy prices remain a sore spot for the economy amid the Iran war and restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, with gas and diesel prices at more than $4 and $6 per gallon on average, respectively.

The average price of a gallon of regular gas is roughly $4.29 as of Friday, 18 cents lower than a month ago but $1.22 higher than a year ago, according to data from AAA .

Consumer sentiment among Republicans and Democrats increased from September to October, while independents’ view of the economy soured, Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers, said in a release.

“While year-ahead business conditions improved about 14%, they stand 16% less than last October’s read,” Hsu noted.

October’s decline in sentiment toward present economic conditions is due to an 18 percent decrease in “buying conditions for durables,” with Hsu citing higher interest rates and “rising concerns about the affordability of such purchases.”

Federal Reserve officials raised interest rates by a quarter point last month, doing so for the first time in three-plus years in a bid to contain inflation . Annual inflation, according to the CPI , has remained above the Fed’s 2 percent target for five and a half years.

Central bank officials will gather again next week to decide whether to hike rates again. Traders are pricing in an 89.5 percent chance of the Fed holding rates at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent, according to the CME FedWatch tool .

Their meeting will come less than a week before the midterm elections , with Democrats looking to pounce on Americans’ worsening outlook of the economy to take control of Congress for President Trump’s remaining two years in office.

articles.title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global cybersecurity alert
articles.summary: Two critical PHP “PHP2Shell” flaws spur global alert, risking unauthenticated remote code execution; millions of internet-facing services may be exposed—patch/upgrade now.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns around the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bug-fix release. The warning follows an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said the flaws posed an urgent risk to organisations relying on websites, customer portals and other web applications.“Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications,” Lakhani said.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers.“Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, security researcher at CloudSEK.Upgrading to a patched PHP version and restarting all PHP processes is the only complete fix for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. Systems running unsupported versions may require vendor-provided updates or migration to supported versions. Interim security measures can reduce exposure but cannot eliminate the risk.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SpaceX wants to be America's fourth phone carrier — tower owners are cashing in
articles.summary: Musk's SpaceX wants to sell you a phone plan, and the companies that own the cell towers are already cashing in.
articles.body:
Elon Musk's SpaceX doesn't just want to beam the internet from space. It wants to sell you a phone plan, and the companies that own the cell towers are already cashing in.

SpaceX ( SPCX ) is in talks for access to at least 80,000 US cell sites, Bloomberg reported Thursday , a step toward building a fourth nationwide carrier .

Crown Castle ( CCI ) is up double digits Friday, with American Tower ( AMT ) and SBA Communications ( SBAC ) close behind. AT&T ( T ) and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) are sliding, and Verizon ( VZ ) is lower too.

The biggest tile on that map is SpaceX itself. At about $2 trillion, it's worth roughly three times all six phone and tower companies combined, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

It's the second time this month the two groups have split this hard. On Oct. 9, SpaceX agreed to pay about $8 billion for a nationwide block of wireless airwaves. Tower stocks jumped, and the carriers sank by double digits that day. Since then, Crown Castle is up 27%, and AT&T is down 14%.

Eighty thousand sites is a big ask. That's about half of the 158,500 cell towers in the US, according to the Wireless Infrastructure Association. American Tower has about 41,000 sites in the US and Canada, and Crown Castle about 40,000.

The landlords' best tenants are the ones getting hurt

AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile bring in about 85% of American Tower's US and Canada revenue. For the tower owners, SpaceX would be a new tenant. For the carriers, it would be a new rival.

The market is pricing that in. The carriers have shed about $21 billion in market value Friday, while the tower stocks have added about $9 billion.

Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant didn't name names on Wednesday's earnings call, but he left the door open. "You can assume that we're talking to all parties," he said.

Nothing is signed yet. The talks are still far from a formal lease deal, and some see them as a bargaining chip in SpaceX's dealings with the carriers. Better satellites could also mean SpaceX needs fewer towers than it's asking for.

The next test comes Tuesday, when American Tower reports earnings. Watch whether management talks up SpaceX as a customer, or whether the rally starts to cool.
